To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the active balancing method can improve the usable energy of serially connected Li-Ion batteries.

the active balancing method can improve the performance of serially connected Li-ion batteries in electric vehicles, and that the performance can be further improved by using the capacity and state of charge as information rather than the voltage.

the active cell balancing method improves the performance of serially connected cells, and that the balancing performance can be further improved by using the state of charge of the cells rather than the voltages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the performance of serially connected Li-ion batteries by actively balancing the cell voltages, the state of charge, and the capacity of each cell.
the development of a novel method of balancing the cells in a serially connected Li-Ion battery stack.
the development of an active balancing method that is based on state of charge and capacity of the cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

active balancing with respect to the state of charge of the cells and with respect to the capacities of the cells can be considered as a good method to improve the performance of a serially connected Li-ion battery stack in electric vehicles, and the method can be implemented with low complexity.
the proposed balancing strategy with the use of state of charge and capacity information is the most effective balancing strategy for serially connected lithium-ion cells in electric vehicles.
the active balancing method is a good method for improving the performance of a serial battery pack in an electric vehicle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and validated an improved active cell balancing method that can be used for serially connected lithium-ion battery stacks in electric vehicles.
the active balancing method using the state of charge of the cells is superior in terms of energy efficiency.
the proposed balancing method is capable of balancing the cells with high accuracy and with low power loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state of charge is a more suitable balancing criterion than the cell voltage, and the capacity of a cell should be taken into account when balancing the cells.
a balancing method using the cell voltage as the balancing variable will lead to a lower energy gain compared to using the cell state of charge and cell capacity.
active balancing with respect to the state of charge can be used to improve the usable energy of a battery stack in an electric vehicle.
